executive_assessment.text: Local vulnerability differs between northern agropastoral systems and flood-exposed Ouémé/coastal systems; broad zones are not presented as commune-level rankings.
Alibori/Atakora insecurity restricts farm, market and mobility access. Named attack examples are dated to the 2025 appraisal, while proposed refugee/host support remains unevaluated.

geographic_notes.text: Southern floods along the Ouémé River and low-lying coast damage crops, displace communities and disrupt infrastructure and market access.
Insecurity in Alibori and Atacora restricts mobility, farm access and markets while driving repeated displacement.
The February 2025 appraisal describes attacks in Matéri and Kérou in Atakora, and Karimama and Banikoara in Alibori, causing school closures and southward movements that pressure host communities.
The February 2025 project document proposes climate-screened water/services infrastructure, livelihood support and participatory planning for refugee and host communities in targeted northern areas.

known_gaps.text: No independently inspected subnational dataset was used to quantify current displacement or insecurity exposure.
The cited climate-risk pathway and economic projections do not provide causal attribution in the inspected passages.
